title: Chessboxing is the perfect body and mind balance.
author: Many_Track4519
selftext:
I’m making Street Chess Boxing, a browser game that alternates chess with arcade boxing. You play a short chess round, get in the ring, then come back to the same position. A checkmate or a KO ends the match.

I used AI image generation for the arenas, character portraits, and combat poses. The hardest part was getting the poses to work together. A kick could look great on its own, but once it followed a guard pose at game speed, the fighter looked like they were swinging around their feet. Lining up the sprites at the feet helped. So did dialing back the extra tilt the game was adding between poses.

The clip is straight gameplay from the browser. It shows some of the chess, all nine arenas, and a few Adventure fights, including a boss that spits a fireball you can jump over.

For anyone using generated sprites in a 2D game, what’s worked best for keeping a character consistent across poses? I’d be especially curious about workflows for keeping proportions stable between the guard, kick, and hit reactions.

You can play it in your browser at [streetchessboxing.com](https://streetchessboxing.com/)
